title: Control Board: a back-off in its wait isn't a hold; a trip only clears by its Resolve
why: decisions/0171 §6's 3c note (Jason, 2026-11-18): "Held or out (a refusal, a refused key, a used-up quota or budget) trips at once"; "a back-off trips at its case limit". The code called a service held for any back-off in its wait, so Wikidata's 429 (issue #26) turned W1's switch-on line red and W1 tripped at 09:00 UTC on 2026-11-19. Now a back-off whose alarm hasn't tripped is paced: its own issue stays a warning and no gate goes red for it. A refusal, a refused key, a used-up quota, or a back-off tripped at its case limit still holds. No rule changes. W1's trip waits for an admin's Check and start again, which now passes in one tap. Also, from Jason's screenshot ("why is the red x still present if the notice says cleared?"): a tripped row offered a bare Start and its Check's notice read "Success", while by 3c only Resolve clears a trip. And control-board-legacy waited 25 minutes in the inbox: the ping got "too soon" and the 10-minute job didn't take it, with nothing on the board to say so.

log.msg: Plan approved (no switch: everyone at once when published), advancing on schedule.
